page: Microsoft Azure D48ns_v6 is a network-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dnv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the D48ns_v6 demonstrates strong performance across multiple categories. Its Passmark CPU score of 61,185.71 and database operations score of 25,284.29 are rated in the top 25%. The processor's support for advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, contributes to strong extended instruction test results. Large-block memory bandwidth is also a highlight, with read speeds reaching 253.44 GB/sec and write speeds at 105.32 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Additionally, the server achieves top-tier performance in small-model LLM text generation, processing 336.16 tokens per second.

The lack of local storage requires reliance on external premium storage options, which represents a key architectural tradeoff for disk-intensive workloads. However, the high memory bandwidth and strong multi-threaded decompression capabilities make it highly efficient for processing-heavy tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high resource density provide reliable performance without the risk of noisy-neighbor resource degradation. This configuration is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference workloads.
